dialogue.origin: こんにちは。相談員です。
dialogue.content: Hello. I'm your counselor.

dialogue.origin: 宜しくお願いします
dialogue.content: Thank you for seeing me.

dialogue.origin: では相談をはじめます。年齢、性別、相談内容を教えてください。
dialogue.content: Alright, let's begin our session. Could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you'd like to discuss?

dialogue.origin: 40歳、女性です
dialogue.content: I'm a 40-year-old woman.

dialogue.origin: 実は、自分の両親と同居しているのですが、
dialogue.content: The thing is, I live with my parents,

dialogue.origin: 父親の事が嫌いで
dialogue.content: and I dislike my father,

dialogue.origin: こんな自分も嫌です
dialogue.content: and I hate myself for feeling this way.

dialogue.origin: どうしていったら良いのかなと思いまして
dialogue.content: I was wondering what I should do about it.

dialogue.origin: 宜しくお願いします
dialogue.content: Thank you for your help.

dialogue.origin: わかりました。お父様の事が嫌いで、そんなご自身も嫌になっているという事ですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So you dislike your father, and you've also come to dislike yourself for feeling that way, is that right?

dialogue.origin: そうなんです
dialogue.content: That's right.

dialogue.origin: 父の歳は80歳です
dialogue.content: My father is 80 years old.

dialogue.origin: 年の変化が出てきています
dialogue.content: Age-related changes are starting to show.

dialogue.origin: 認知は大丈夫ですが、身体の動きが
dialogue.content: He doesn't have dementia, but his physical movements...

dialogue.origin: 若い時と違って、パッパッとは動けないのは承知しています
dialogue.content: ...I know he can't move as quickly as he did when he was younger.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: でも、ご飯をボロボロこぼしたり
dialogue.content: But he spills food all over the place when he eats,

dialogue.origin: トイレの蓋が閉まっているのに、そのまま腰掛けて排尿したり
dialogue.content: or he'll sit down and urinate on the closed toilet lid.

dialogue.origin: ほんとにヤダです
dialogue.content: I really can't stand it.

dialogue.origin: 確かに高齢の方と一緒に暮らすのは、大変な事も多いしそれが原因で嫌になったりしますよね。
dialogue.content: I can certainly see how living with an elderly person can be challenging and lead to these kinds of feelings.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです
dialogue.content: Yes, exactly.

dialogue.origin: もっと、ひどくなるのかと思うと、気持ちがとても沈みます
dialogue.content: When I think about it getting worse, I feel so down.

dialogue.origin: 自分の親なのに
dialogue.content: Even though he's my own father...

dialogue.origin: 介護出来るかも、不安です
dialogue.content: I'm worried about whether I'll be able to care for him.

dialogue.origin: 歳だと思って、諦めるしかないのでしょうか？
dialogue.content: Should I just chalk it up to his age and give up?

dialogue.origin: 要介護ではないので、施設入所は無理です
dialogue.content: He doesn't qualify for nursing care, so moving him into a facility isn't an option.

dialogue.origin: コロナ禍でもあるので、通所も控えたいです
dialogue.content: And with the COVID-19 pandemic, I'd prefer to avoid day services as well.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。入所は難しい状況なんですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So moving him into a facility isn't a viable option right now.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです
dialogue.content: That's right.

dialogue.origin: 主人も、仕方ないとは言ってくれています
dialogue.content: My husband also tells me that it can't be helped.

dialogue.origin: もう少し、可愛らしいお爺さんでいたらなと思います。
dialogue.content: I just wish he were a bit more of a sweet, endearing old man.

dialogue.origin: 家族の方も現状の理解はあるんですね。
dialogue.content: It sounds like your family understands the situation.

dialogue.origin: そうですね
dialogue.content: Yes, they are.

dialogue.origin: おじい様とは普段の会話・やり取りでも気になる点があるのですか？
dialogue.content: Are there things that bother you in your daily conversations and interactions with your father as well?

dialogue.origin: 私が父の事を怒らないようにと、母は先回りして注意しています
dialogue.content: My mother preemptively warns him so that I don't get angry at my father.

dialogue.origin: 日本語がヘタです
dialogue.content: I'm not explaining this well.

dialogue.origin: 大丈夫ですよ。思いついたままの表現でいいですよ。
dialogue.content: That's all right. Please feel free to express yourself however it comes to you.

dialogue.origin: ご飯の時に、『おかずここにもあるよ』と伝えると、『お腹一杯、終わった。』と言いながら、食事しています
dialogue.content: During meals, if I tell him, 'There are more side dishes here,' he'll say, 'I'm full, I'm done,' while he's still eating.

dialogue.origin: おかしくないですか？
dialogue.content: Isn't that strange?

dialogue.origin: こういう風に、返事すると良いよと伝えますがダメですね
dialogue.content: I try to tell him how he could respond, but it's no use.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。改善されないのですね。
dialogue.content: I see. So it doesn't get any better.

dialogue.origin: 長いこと生きてきたから、今更かわらないですよね
dialogue.content: He's lived for so long, I guess he's not going to change now.

dialogue.origin: 私が変われば良いのかな
dialogue.content: Maybe I'm the one who needs to change.

dialogue.origin: 目の前で、犬飼いしている姿は見たくないです
dialogue.content: I don't want to see him eating like a dog right in front of me.

dialogue.origin: どうして犬食いかというと、食器にかぶさって食べれば、口からこぼれても食器に落ちると…
dialogue.content: The reason he eats like a dog is because if he hunches over his plate, even if food falls from his mouth, it lands back in the dish...

dialogue.origin: 本人なりの理由があるんですよね
dialogue.content: He has his own reasons, I suppose.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。そういう姿は見たくないですね。
dialogue.content: I can understand why you wouldn't want to see that.

dialogue.origin: そうなんです
dialogue.content: Exactly.

dialogue.origin: 口一杯に頬張るからいけないと思うんです。飲み込む前に、さらに口に入れる
dialogue.content: I think it's because he stuffs his mouth full. He puts more food in before he's even swallowed.

dialogue.origin: 口の中のものが落ちないように、啜るわけです
dialogue.content: So, he slurps to keep the food from falling out of his mouth.

dialogue.origin: カレーを啜るって見たことあります？
dialogue.content: Have you ever seen someone slurp curry?

dialogue.origin: そうなんですね。見た事ないですね。
dialogue.content: Oh, I see. No, I haven't seen that.

dialogue.origin: そうでしょ
dialogue.content: Right?

dialogue.origin: 確かに、啜れば口からは落ちない
dialogue.content: Sure, if he slurps, it doesn't fall out of his mouth,

dialogue.origin: でもね
dialogue.content: But still...

dialogue.origin: 注意しても、改善しないし
dialogue.content: even if I point it out, he doesn't change,

dialogue.origin: 父を見ないように、ご飯を食べています
dialogue.content: so I eat my meals trying not to look at my father.

dialogue.origin: 一緒に住んでいてそういう姿を見るのはつらいですね。
dialogue.content: It must be painful to see that when you live together.

dialogue.origin: これに、認知が入ったらどうしましょう
dialogue.content: What am I going to do if dementia sets in on top of this?

dialogue.origin: そうですね。不安ですよね。
dialogue.content: Yes, that must be a worry.

dialogue.origin: 不安です
dialogue.content: I am worried.

dialogue.origin: 70歳の母もいますし
dialogue.content: And there's my 70-year-old mother, too.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。お母さまもそういう事になる可能性はありますよね。
dialogue.content: I see. So it's possible the same thing could happen with your mother.

dialogue.origin: そうなんですよね
dialogue.content: That's right.

dialogue.origin: なってほしくはないけど
dialogue.content: I don't want it to happen, but...

dialogue.origin: そうですね。なってほしくないですね。
dialogue.content: Of course. We don't want that to happen.

dialogue.origin: 大変さが増すだけでなく、自分の母のそういう姿は見たくないですね
dialogue.content: It's not just that it would be more difficult; I don't want to see my own mother like that.

dialogue.origin: ええ、家族のそうなった姿は見てるだけでも辛いですよね。
dialogue.content: Yes, it's painful just to watch a family member go through that.

dialogue.origin: 辛いですね
dialogue.content: It is painful.

dialogue.origin: 親は、いつまでも元気でいて欲しいです
dialogue.content: I want my parents to stay healthy forever.

dialogue.origin: 元気な姿が一番いいですよね。ものすごくご両親思いなんですね。
dialogue.content: It's best when they are healthy, isn't it? You care about your parents very much.

dialogue.origin: そう言われると、こそばゆいです
dialogue.content: It feels a little embarrassing to hear you say that.

dialogue.origin: 自分が完璧主義なのかな？
dialogue.content: I wonder if I'm a perfectionist.

dialogue.origin: だから、父の行動が許せないのかもしれない
dialogue.content: Maybe that's why I can't tolerate my father's behavior.

dialogue.origin: あと、少しの人生、穏やかに暮らして欲しい
dialogue.content: For the few years he has left, I want him to live peacefully.

dialogue.origin: と、いうか、私が穏やかに暮らしたい
dialogue.content: Or rather, I want to live peacefully myself.

dialogue.origin: そうですね。穏やかに過ごしたいですね。
dialogue.content: Yes, it makes sense that you want to live peacefully.

dialogue.origin: 穏やかに
dialogue.content: Peacefully.

dialogue.origin: どうすれば穏やかな気持ちになれそうですか？
dialogue.content: What do you think might help you feel more at peace?

dialogue.origin: 相手に感謝の気持ちを持つことかな
dialogue.content: Maybe having a sense of gratitude toward him.

dialogue.origin: いくら、嫌でも、ここまで育ててくれた訳だし
dialogue.content: No matter how much I dislike him now, he did raise me, after all.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。そうですね、大切なご両親ですものね。
dialogue.content: I see. That's right; they are your parents, after all.

dialogue.origin: 自分の気持ちしだいですね
dialogue.content: It depends on my own mindset, doesn't it?

dialogue.origin: 父に優しく出来た日は、自分にご褒美をあげようかな
dialogue.content: Maybe on days when I manage to be kind to my father, I'll give myself a little reward.

dialogue.origin: そうですね。気持ち・考え次第でもあると思います。
dialogue.content: That's right. I think a lot of it does depend on your feelings and mindset.

dialogue.origin: そうですね
dialogue.content: I agree.

dialogue.origin: ご自身へのご褒美も考えると楽しくなりそうですね。
dialogue.content: Thinking about rewards for yourself might make things feel a bit more enjoyable.

dialogue.origin: ご褒美は、何にしようかな
dialogue.content: I wonder what my reward should be.

dialogue.origin: 楽しみを考えるのはいいですね。
dialogue.content: It's good to have something to look forward to.

dialogue.origin: 楽しみを考えながら、生活してみようかな
dialogue.content: Maybe I'll try to live my life while thinking about things to look forward to.

dialogue.origin: 途中ですか、以上で終了します。お疲れ様でした。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.content: I'm sorry to cut this short, but our session is over for today. Thank you for your time.

dialogue.origin: ありがとうございました。聞いてもらって少し楽になりました。
dialogue.content: Thank you very much. I feel a little better after being heard.

topic.sub: 両親との同居におけるストレスと介護への不安
